memories.content: Conduct one review prior to submission focusing solely on the validity of user problems, design interventions, and evaluation logic.
Cross-check whether research questions align with the core functions of the prototype.
Cross-check whether evaluation tasks align with representative measures.
Cross-check whether collected evidence aligns with design and operational decisions to be changed.
Verify at the end that user problems, design interventions, user studies, and expected contributions form a coherent logical flow.
HCI reviewers view the validity of design interventions as low if research questions are not linked to prototype functions.
HCI reviewers view the validity of evaluation plans as low if evaluation tasks do not produce representative measures.
HCI reviewers view the practicality of contributions as low if collected evidence cannot change design or operational decisions.
Cross-check at the end whether each research question, formative evaluation data, and design modification judgment are seamlessly connected.
Review whether the application conditions of proposed design principles and boundary cases of failure are presented together.
The user can have contributions reviewed only if prototype outcomes and the transferable design knowledge derived from them are separated.
The scope of observation in controlled formative evaluations does not include long-term adaptation and operational changes in real-world usage contexts.
Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Trace back the resources required for each core prototype feature and field research procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility by examining the personnel required for each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility by examining the equipment required for each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility by examining the time required for each procedure.
Document separately the commitments and confirmation status of field partners required for recruitment, installation, and operational support.
Designate a responsible party for software updates, equipment inspections, and user support during the deployment period.
The user's deployment readiness can be assessed only when dependencies on external services and field personnel are visible.
Field schedules and assigned personnel may change due to operational factors beyond the researcher’s control.

analysis.overview: The frames address complementary but separate review concerns: the reference frame concentrates on research and contribution validity, while the compared frame concentrates on deployment feasibility, dependency visibility, and operational accountability. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other’s substantive claims.

relations.reason: This establishes a one-sided review stage and focus with no scope-aligned feasibility counterpart in the compared frame.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers transparent uncertainty, resource-based feasibility, partner and service dependencies, deployment responsibilities, and operational volatility affecting schedules and personnel.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers pre-submission validity review, alignment among questions, prototype functions, measures, evidence, and design changes, coherent contribution logic, principle boundaries, separation of outcomes from transferable knowledge, and limits of controlled formative evaluation.
